title: Abraham and the Covenant
objective: After this level you can explain the covenant Jews believe God made with Abraham, and why Judaism, Christianity and Islam all honor him.
summary: Jews believe God made an everlasting covenant with Abraham, promising land and descendants, with circumcision as its sign. Judaism, Christianity and Islam all trace their story to him.

cards.headline: Three of the world's faiths trace their story to one man on the move.
cards.body: Judaism, Christianity and Islam all honor Abraham. For Jews he is where something specific begins: a covenant, a binding bond with God. Here is what Genesis says was promised, and the sign that still marks it.

cards.headline: Pack up, destination unknown
cards.body: Genesis tells how God spoke to Abram: "Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto the land that I will show thee." He left Ur, in Mesopotamia, and only later learned the land was Canaan. Picture loading the car with no address in the map app. Abraham is best known for exactly this: the depth of his faith.

cards.headline: A covenant, not a contract
cards.body: A covenant (Hebrew berit) is a binding agreement, and in this one God binds himself by oath. Jewish tradition holds that God promised Abraham the land of Canaan and descendants beyond counting. Genesis even renames him: Abram becomes Abraham, "the father of a multitude of nations." And it calls the bond "an everlasting covenant", for Abraham "and thy seed after thee throughout their generations."

cards.headline: A sign in the body
cards.body: Genesis 17 names the covenant's sign: every male is to be circumcised, "a token of a covenant", at eight days old. Jewish families still hold the rite, berit mila (often spelled brit milah), on a baby boy's eighth day, with blessings and the giving of his name. In Judaism it represents the fulfillment of the covenant between God and Abraham. One promise, marked again in each generation.

cards.headline: Three faiths, one ancestor
cards.body: Remember Level 8's family tree? Jews and Christians trace the story through Abraham's son Isaac, Muslims through his son Ishmael. In Islam, the Prophet Muhammad is a descendant of Ishmael; in Christianity, the genealogy of Jesus is traced to Isaac. One ancestor, three family stories, each told in its own words.

cards.headline: Abraham and the Covenant: the takeaways
learned: Jews believe God made a covenant with Abraham: land and descendants
Circumcision on the eighth day is the covenant's sign
Judaism, Christianity and Islam all trace their story to Abraham

questions.prompt: According to Genesis 17, what is the sign of God's covenant with Abraham?

options.label: Lighting candles every Friday evening
options.rationale: That is a Sabbath custom, not the covenant sign.

options.label: A yearly pilgrimage back to Ur
options.rationale: Abraham left Ur; no return is commanded.

options.label: Circumcision of every male at eight days old
Building an altar in every home
options.rationale: Genesis 17 names circumcision as the sign.

questions.explanation: Genesis 17 calls circumcision "a token of a covenant", performed when a boy is eight days old.

questions.prompt: In Jewish tradition, what did God promise Abraham in the covenant?

options.label: The land of Canaan and descendants beyond counting
Victory over Egypt's pharaoh
options.rationale: That belongs to the later Exodus story.

options.label: A written law code carved in stone
options.rationale: The law comes later, at Sinai.

options.label: Great wealth and a long life in Ur
options.rationale: He was called to leave Ur.

questions.explanation: Abraham was promised the land of Canaan and numerous descendants, in "an everlasting covenant".

questions.prompt: Judaism, Christianity and Islam trace different family lines from Abraham. Which pairing is right?

options.label: Jews through Ishmael; Muslims through Isaac
options.rationale: It is the other way round.

options.label: Christians through Ishmael; Muslims through Isaac
options.rationale: Christians trace the line through Isaac.

options.label: All three through Moses
options.rationale: Moses comes much later in the story.

options.label: Jews and Christians through Isaac; Muslims through Ishmael

questions.explanation: Jews and Christians trace the story through Isaac; in Islam, Muhammad descends from Ishmael.
